title: Manuscript Cataloguing, Metadata & TEI XML Fundamentals
query: How do RDF linked-data models and TEI Header schemas structure manuscript metadata and document validation in digital scholarly editions, and how do rule-based validation and AI metadata enrichment compare?

results.title: Automatic Metadata Extraction Leveraging Large Language Models in Digital Humanities
results.authors_venue_year: [HTML][HTML] Automatic Metadata Extraction Leveraging Large Language Models in Digital HumanitiesA Morejón, B Navarro-Colorado, C García-Barceló… - Electronics, 2025 - mdpi.comExplores aligning the domain-specific TEI standard for text encoding in digital humanities with the cross-domain DCAT standard, which facilitates adherence to FAIR principles for metadata structure.Interoperability and Silos: Highlights that DCAT-based approaches enable richer cross-domain interoperability, improved machine-readability, and seamless integration of digital humanities data, contrasting with TEI’s focus on project-specific metadata that often leads to isolated silos.Rule-Based vs LLM Enrichment: Proposes a hybrid pipeline combining expert mapping rules and automated metadata generation with Large Language Models (LLMs) to facilitate the inclusion and discovery of literary works in interoperable infrastructures, comparing rule-based limitations against LLM scalability.Save Cite Cited by 2 Related articles All 4 versions  Cached [PDF] arxiv.org

results.title: Position paper: metadata enrichment model: Integrating neural networks and semantic knowledge graphs for cultural heritage applications
results.authors_venue_year: Position paper: metadata enrichment model: Integrating neural networks and semantic knowledge graphs for cultural heritage applicationsJ Ignatowicz, K Kutt, GJ Nalepa - 2025 International Joint …, 2025 - ieeexplore.ieee.orgPresents the Metadata Enrichment Model (MEM) as a conceptual framework that enriches metadata for digitized collections by combining fine-tuned computer vision models, large language models (LLMs), and structured knowledge graphs.Semantic Knowledge Graphs: Explains that the MEM framework links enriched metadata to external databases by creating knowledge graphs, thereby enabling cross-institutional querying and integration, which is crucial for Linked Data-wise metadata.Rule-Based and AI Checks: Describes the Multilayer Vision Mechanism (MVM) that uses LLMs for decision-making and combines the output with rule-based checks, such as minimum pixel size or confidence thresholds, to determine if further visual analysis is required.Save Cite Cited by 7 Related articles All 6 versions  No full text available [PDF] ieee.orgCheck for full text @ X

results.title: Metadata integration: A systematic review on methods, challenges and applications across multiple domains
results.authors_venue_year: Metadata integration: A systematic review on methods, challenges and applications across multiple domainsRBD De Oliveira, SN Alves-Souza - IEEE Access, 2025 - ieeexplore.ieee.orgExplains that RDF graphs offer a foundational structure for encoding metadata as triples, which can be merged, validated, and aligned, supporting exploration and discovery by allowing navigation of conceptual neighborhoods.Rule-Based Validation: Notes that rule-based metadata integration relies on the explicit specification of rules to align, transform, and unify heterogeneous metadata, often employing constraint languages like SHACL to validate, transform, or infer new metadata statements.AI Metadata Enrichment Comparison: Identifies AI-based approaches as extending beyond traditional rule-based methods by using techniques like Natural Language Processing (NLP) to interpret free text metadata, identify semantic similarities, and connect terms to controlled vocabularies or ontologies, thereby reducing dependency on manual curation for semantic enrichment.Save Cite Cited by 3 Related articles All 2 versions  [PDF] wiley.comCheck for full text @ X

results.title: Harmonizing and publishing heterogeneous premodern manuscript metadata as Linked Open Data
results.authors_venue_year: Harmonizing and publishing heterogeneous premodern manuscript metadata as Linked Open DataM Koho, T Burrows, E Hyvönen, E Ikkala… - Journal of the …, 2022 - Wiley Online LibraryDiscusses the creation of a unified data model, a Linked Open Data (LOD) knowledge graph, and a Semantic Web portal to integrate distinct manuscript datasets for comprehensive research, addressing challenges posed by incompatible data silos.Data Model and Pipeline: Explains that a unified data model, a repeatable data transformation pipeline, a Linked Open Data knowledge graph, and a Semantic Web portal were major products used to harmonize and publish heterogeneous premodern manuscript metadata.TEI Tagging Structure: Notes that the source data included XML files—digital transcriptions of historical manuscript catalogs annotated with TEI tags to mark up structured data elements—which gave structure to the manuscript descriptions.Save Cite Cited by 40 Related articles All 25 versions  [PDF] uni-heidelberg.de

results.title: Linked Open Data and manuscript descriptions
results.authors_venue_year: Linked Open Data and manuscript descriptionsB Bauer, R Bleier, J Sonnberger - Das Mittelalter …, 2025 - heiup.uni-heidelberg.deExplains that Linked Open Data principles, including Tim Berners-Lee’s five-star LOD model and technologies such as RDF, underpin the Semantic Web and are used to provide structured data availability for manuscript descriptions in the humanities.TEI and Semantic Web: Details the role of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI) in creating machine-readable manuscript descriptions and preparing data for the Semantic Web, noting that TEI standards are important for libraries, archives, and digital scholarly editions.AI and Data Relevance: Notes that recent developments in machine learning and Artificial Intelligence (AI) strongly emphasize the relevance of data for research, including in the humanities, potentially impacting metadata enrichment.Save Cite Cited by 2 Related articles All 4 versions  No full text available View as HTML [PDF] openedition.org

results.title: Formal ontologies, linked data, and TEI semantics
results.authors_venue_year: Formal ontologies, linked data, and TEI semanticsF Ciotti, F Tomasi - Journal of the Text Encoding Initiative, 2016 - journals.openedition.orgProposes an ontological extension of the TEI framework to partially formalize the semantics of its markup constructs, providing a formal definition to the implicit concepts underlying XML text encoding.Benefits of Formal Semantics: Explains that furnishing the TEI with a semantics based on a formal ontology facilitates the management and research of document collections and aids interoperability with other standards in digital cultural heritage contexts.TEI to Linked Data: Details a model for exposing both the TEI semantic model and individual TEI documents as Linked Data through a conversion process involving the creation of an RDF triple store.Save Cite Cited by 77 Related articles All 8 versions  No full text available View as HTML [PDF] bsz-bw.de

results.title: Metadata for research data
results.authors_venue_year: Metadata for research dataT Trippel - Harmonising Language Data: Standards for Linguistic …, 2025 - books.google.comExplains that metadata can be embedded in research data, specifically mentioning the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI) where metadata is located in the mandatory TEI header of XML files, thus structuring digital scholarly editions.RDF and Linked Data: Notes that when metadata is serialized in JSON-LD or another RDF format, the resulting linked data can reference the schema.org vocabulary, relating RDF linked-data models to semantic enrichment.Metadata Generation Process: Indicates that metadata in the TEI header can be included through a human-driven annotation process or via automatic generation, suggesting ways metadata enrichment and entry are performed for scholarly data.Save Cite Cited by 6 Related articles All 5 versions  No full text available [PDF] unisalento.it

results.title: Automating XML-TEI Encoding of Unpublished Correspondence
results.authors_venue_year: Automating XML-TEI Encoding of Unpublished CorrespondenceM De Cristofaro, D Zilio - Umanistica Digitale, 2025 - iris.unisalento.itDescribes how the data model structure for the digital scholarly edition was inspired by four different projects, including the Darwin Correspondence Project and the Bellini Digital Correspondence.Linked Data Structure: Explains that data is structured in a macro XML file, and individual letter files are linked to this macro file using attributes like `@ref` for person and organization names, supporting linked data principles.AI vs. Manual Encoding: Compares automated encoding using Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT-4 and Claude 3.5 Sonnet to manual XML-TEI encoding to assess accuracy and the ability of LLMs to extract metadata, ensuring structural validity, and associating correct references from a master file.Save Cite Cited by 2 Related articles All 6 versions  No full text available View as HTML [PDF] acm.orgFull View

results.title: Wikibase model for premodern manuscript metadata harmonization, linked data integration, and discovery
results.authors_venue_year: Wikibase model for premodern manuscript metadata harmonization, linked data integration, and discoveryM Koho, LP Coladangelo, L Ransom… - ACM Journal on …, 2023 - dl.acm.orgDescribes the Digital Scriptorium 2.0 (DS 2.0) data model for premodern manuscript metadata harmonization, which is based on Linked Open Data (LOD) practices and technologies using Wikibase.Structure of the Data Model: Explains that the DS 2.0 data model is object-centric, focusing on the main manuscript metadata record as the focal point, to which most of the metadata is attached in a star-like manner, contrasting it with an event-based model like the Mapping Manuscript Migrations (MMM) project.Metadata Enrichment and Validation: Details the process of semantic enrichment by matching existing string values in metadata records to structured counterparts in linked data authorities and vocabularies, such as TGN and Wikidata, using OpenRefine for reconciliation.Save Cite Cited by 17 Related articles All 6 versions  No full text available

results.authors_venue_year: [BOOK][B] Ontotext GraphDB in Practice: The Complete Guide for Developers and EngineersW Smith - 2025 - books.google.comExplains that RDF-based graph databases are suitable for handling the fluidity and extensibility of metadata schemas required for evolving publishing standards, and details the use of flexible ontologies like the Publishing Ontology (PCO) or FOAF to represent authorship and content provenance semantically.Ingestion Pipeline Structure: Outlines how data ingestion pipelines harmonize metadata from multiple sources, including manuscripts, into a unified RDF graph, supporting lineage tracking, recommendation engines, and enhanced discoverability in digital platforms.Rule-Based Validation: Discusses that constraint validation with SHACL is typically employed after transformation and enrichment to check for structural or semantic aberrations, and mentions that advanced rule-based logic can be incorporated for complex business requirements.Save Cite Related articles All 2 versions  No full text available Looking for more results...Scholar Labs is currently not designed for queries like this.Suggestions:Try a different questionTry your query on Google ScholarNo results found.Search stopped.Looking for results...Scholar Labs is currently not designed for queries like this.Suggestions:Try a different questionTry your query on Google ScholarNo results found.Search stopped.An error occurred.RetryMore resultsReady to explore your own questions and answers?Ask your questionScholar Labs is experimental and can make mistakes.Help & PrivacyPrivacyTermsHelpYou're on the waitlistScholar Labs home
